newsitem.title: GERMANY: Banks lash out at collapse of German tax reform.
newsitem.headline: Banks lash out at collapse of German tax reform.

text.p: Germany's private banks on Thursday lashed out at Bonn's politicians for having gambled away the chance to reform taxes, a plan said to have been pivotal for the country's economic health.

Martin Kohlhaussen, head of the Federal Association of German Banks, said politicians acted irresponsibly by preferring to make tactical, political decisions rather than concentrating on the chance to reform the tax system.
Kohlhaussen, who is also the management board chairman at Commerzbank AG, said Finance Minister Theo Waigel's ambitious tax reform plans had been widely supported by private industry.
"The fact that Germany would profit from this reform should have been quite clear to everybody," he said.
The association warned that without a comprehensive tax reform there would be no economic upswing, no solution to the grave labour market problems and also no way out of the budget crisis.
He added: "The politicians who have driven the plans to collapse are clearly not aware of the responsibility they bear for Germany as an economic site."
The banking association represents Germany's private banks.
